div.head: Northu Inscr.
div.ab: The law of the Northumbrian priests
div.note: Liebermann's text is from D (Cambridge, Corpus Christi College 201, p. 43, after ‘Polity’ 25, in the same hand, c. 1060), the same manuscript as the modern edition. The heading is in red. Liebermann dates the text 1028–c. 1060 and places it at York. Clause number standardised from ‘Northu. Inscr.’.; AU: corrected against Rabin p. 302 / 303, October 2026 (was “Norðhymbra preosta lagu”, now “Norðhymbra preosta lagu (expanded letters in italics: Norðhymbra preosta lagu)”); W: corrected against Rabin p. 303, October 2026 (was “∅; Priests'”, now “The; Priests’”); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads); Wormald, Making of English Law I, October 2026 (was “1028–c.1060; probably 1020–23 (Whitelock)”, now “1028–c.1060 (Liebermann); probably 1020–23 (Whitelock); after 1023 (Wormald)”); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date at the head of the text); Wormald, Making of English Law I, October 2026 (was “1028–c.1060 (Liebermann); probably 1020–23 (Whitelock); after 1023 (Wormald)”, now “1028–c.1060 (Liebermann, I p. 380); probably 1020–23 (Whitelock); after 1023 (Wormald, MEL pp. 396–7)”); BQ: page of each of Liebermann’s texts and of his German, checked against Liebermann, Gesetze I (our double-read transcription), October 2026 (e.g. was “(empty)”, now “D 380; German 380”; 80 rows of Northu)
Manuscripts: D = Cambridge, Corpus Christi College MS 201, pp. 43–46.

Die Überschrift bezieht sich wahrscheinlich nur auf Teil I. Dann kann sie original sein; s. o. Einl. 2
The heading probably refers only to Part I. In that case it may be original; see above Introduction 2

Der Gen. pl. Northymbra bezeichnet sowohl die Gegend wie die Laienbewohnerschaft, über welche die Priester Pfarrgewalt üben, nicht etwa die Nationalität der Priester.—Der Gen. preosta ist subjektiv: ‘durch sie [nicht bloss ‘für, über sie’] gegebenes Gesetz’; s. o. Einl. 10. Derselbe Begriff heisst u. 2, 3 preostlagu

The gen. pl. Northymbra denotes both the region and the lay population over which the priests exercise parochial authority, not, say, the nationality of the priests. — The gen. preosta is subjective: ‘law given by them’ [not merely ‘for them, about them’]; see above Introduction 10. The same concept is called preostlagu below 2, 3
